findings: ARCHITECTURE (binding): __HARNESS.screenshot() is canvas.toDataURL(). game/src/render/ui.js draws into an offscreen 2D canvas and composites it as a textured quad. W1-21 follows it exactly: Renderer.menus = new UISurface(w,h), composited after the dialogue surface and before the title surface. NO DOM anywhere in this interface.

Renderer.setSize() resizes the UI canvas to the drawing buffer, so texel:pixel is 1:1 and there is nothing to upscale — that is what makes RI-UIX06 M-F17.2 (DPR-2 stem sharpness) passable from a canvas path. Texture filters are NearestFilter both ways; a LINEAR filter on a 1:1 blit would soften every glyph for nothing.

DESIGN DECISION, contradicts the dispatch brief: THERE IS NO MAP SCREEN. openMenu('map') throws with the reason. The brief said 'the map is Morrowind's and has no quest pins'; RI-UIX04 JU8 says 'map unreachable AND non-existent', calls the existence half the one that matters, and makes a map a hard fail plus AR-2 via Q7. RI-UIX02 §F's own compromise is taken instead: the compass is a boxed ITEM (shore-compass) you stop and open, and the charts are a pilot's PROSE directions (pilots-chart-book) read on the book screen. Both are objects with weight in the inventory. A critic may overrule this; the route is a seam ruling, not a code change.

DATA DEFECT FIXED: game/data/progression/levels.json carried soul_cost_formula 'round(0.02L^3+3.06L^2+105.6L-895)', which is NEGATIVE below level 9, plus a 5-row table whose values (673,689,706,723) are the DARK SOULS reference column of RI-PRG01's table, not ours, plus a 6-name Souls attribute list contradicting attributes.json's ten. The level-up screen showed souls-to-next = 0 at level 6 and RI-UIX03 L3 was unpassable by any build. Replaced with RI-PRG01's canonical formula and its own 139-row table; formula and table agree on all 139 rows.

CONSUMPTION FIXED: burden. burdenTierOf/_burdenMult/traversal.step consumed sim.player.burdenRatio every frame, and the ONLY thing that ever set it was the harness verb setBurden(). Carrying 44 objects cost nothing. Engine._recomputeBurden() now sets it from the same weight sum the inventory screen prints, every step. Perturbation: adding the hauberk + maul moves the tier and _burdenMult() returns 0.90, which sim/traversal.js applies as a speed.

MARKER-SCAN DEPARTURE, declared: RI-UIX02 §B's F2 key regex /(pos|coord|location|xyz|latlon)/i is an unanchored substring and returns 300 hits on the shipped tree, ALL of them the word 'disposition'. Matched as a word instead; self-test asserts target_pos / destination_coord / position / poi_location / xyz still fire and disposition / composition do not.

One declared marker-scan exception: stealth/detection.json:no_meter.hud_elements = 0 (F1's hud_.* branch catching W1-15's DECLARATION that stealth draws no HUD elements). Recorded in tools/analysis/marker-scan-exceptions.json with what removes it; a stale declaration fails the run.

getUIState() rewritten. It BUILDS the layout for the current frame before reporting, because every probe runs setRenderRate(0) and a HUD that only existed during a render would report the frame before last to RI-UIX01 D1 ('100% of frames within ±0.005').
Measured at 1920x1080, ui-journal fixture: HUD 6 persistent elements, union coverage 2.0457% of frame (RI-UIX01 §C budget 4.0%, hard fail 8.0%). Menu panel area_frac 0.5718 (P5 cap 0.60).
Pause rule measured: openMenu('inventory') out of combat, stepFrames(120), getFrame() 0 -> 0. In-combat behaviour still to be measured.

Journal measured: 19 entries declared as elements in chronological order, 12 visible on the spread, interleave_ratio 0.8889 (JU2 bar 0.5, hard fail 0.30; the grouped-view ceiling for a 5-quest/19-entry fixture is 0.222). uiSearch('ledger') returns 1 result, chronological true.

Book layout retuned twice against RI-UIX05 §A: 26 px type, leading 1.46, 46-65 chars/line, full pages 112-172 words. The per-BOOK words/page median is ~102, below B1's 120-180, because half the shipped readables are 100-150 word notes — the library is W1-17's and RI-LOR03's median book is ~520 words. Declared content gap, not a layout defect: the FULL pages are in band.

CONTRAST BUG FOUND AND FIXED by looking at the render: the inventory drew iron-gall ink (L 0.014) on a reed ground (L 0.038) = 1.4:1, unreadable. chrome.js now derives the ink from the ground's luminance and every screen asks for ink()/inkDim(); paperContrast() reports the pair it chose.

PROVEN: __HARNESS.screenshot() and page.screenshot() are byte-identical. ui-layer.mjs at 8 viewpoints (world, combat, and all six screens), 1280x720, buffer pinned 1:1: 0 differing pixels at every one. The interface is entirely inside the canvas; there is no DOM in it.
K2 (RI-UIX02 §C undeclared components) = 0 across 8 viewpoints at the 1920-buffer run. The rerun at a 1:1 1280 buffer exposed a REAL BUG rather than a measurement artefact (next finding).

BUG FOUND BY THE PIXEL SWEEP AND FIXED: THREE.CanvasTexture allocates GPU storage at the canvas's size on first upload and re-uploads with texSubImage2D. Resizing the UI canvas (1920x1080 -> 1280x720) pasted the new frame into the BOTTOM-LEFT of the still-1920 texture (WebGL origin) and left the old frame in the rest, so the player saw TWO interfaces: the correct one and a ghost of the previous size, offset up the screen. Measured: the ghost's quick-slot cluster at (773,643) instead of (1152,592) — exactly where the arithmetic puts it. Fix: texture.dispose() in UISurface.setSize(). It is invisible at a fixed resolution and appears on every window resize, every orientation change and every DPR-2 capture. game/src/render/ui.js (W1-07's dialogue surface) has the same shape of resize without a dispose and is likely to carry the same defect.

RI-UIX01 measured (ui-census, arena_duel, in combat, 1920x1080, 600 frames): persistent 6, peak total 7, HUD union coverage 2.0457% (budget 4.0%, hard fail 8.0%), with conditionals 2.1568% (budget 6.5%), CENTRE 50%x50% coverage 0.0000%, world-anchored [hud.lockon] only, numeric text [hud.heal] only. §D1 max |error| 0.000000 over 600 frames, 0% out of tolerance, tween_runs 0, spend visible on the frame in 5/5 spends. 11/11.

RI-UIX04 measured (journal-ui, ui-journal fixture): 11/11. interleave_ratio 0.8889 from RENDER ORDER (bar 0.5; the grouped-view ceiling for a 19-entry/5-quest fixture is 0.2222; the date-interleaved ideal is 0.8000). openMenu('map') throws, 'map' is in neither navigable[] nor listMenus().

RI-UIX03 measured (ui-pause): M-P1 frame delta 0 of 120 out of combat; M-P2 frame delta EXACTLY 120 of 120 in combat; P8 37 steps = 37 frames; P4 0/30 before aggro and 60/60 after with the screen still open; P5 opacity 0.50, panel area 57.2%, world still visible in 95.7% of centre-40% pixels; E11 no toast in a fight; all seven surfaces open and draw.

BUG FOUND BY RI-UIX03 P5's PERTURBATION TEST AND FIXED: per-element globalAlpha COMPOUNDS. Drawing a panel, a header, a divider and a row each at 0.5 composites to 1-0.5^4 = 0.94, so a screen that DECLARED 55% opacity was opaque over its own centre. Measured: with the inventory open in a fight, a setTimeOfDay 13->1 perturbation moved 99.8% of the pixels outside the screen and 0.0% of the centre 40%x40% pixels under it. Fixed with UISurface.beginScreen()/endScreen(): elements paint at full alpha and the whole screen rectangle is knocked back once with a destination-in wash, which touches nothing outside it so the HUD keeps full opacity. The first version of the occlusion check compared composited-vs-world luminance and PASSED this build at 95.7%; the perturbation version is what caught it.

MEASUREMENT DEFECTS IN MY OWN TOOLS, found and fixed rather than shipped: (1) ui-metrics counted whole samples for the stem transition, which returns 1 for a HARD-ALIASED edge and 2 for a correctly antialiased one — inverting the metric, since M-F17.5 wants AA present. Now interpolated to sub-pixels. (2) FD3 tested >=18 px at 720p, which fails a correctly proportional layout; B4's absolute leg is a 1080p leg and the fractional leg applies everywhere. (3) The alpha-fringing scan swept the panel INTERIOR and reported a glyph stem (legitimately darker than both neighbours) as a 156-unit halo; it now samples only the UI's silhouette against the world.

EVENT VOCABULARY AMENDED (AM-W1-21-01, game/src/sim/events.js): equip_start, equip_end, item_used, item_moved. RI-UIX03 P7's method is 'assert the trace shows a committed state of >=30 frames with iframe:false' and there was no event that could carry it.

RI-UIX03 FINAL (tools/harness/ui-pause.mjs, ui-journal, 1280x720): 10/10. M-P1 0 of 120 out of combat; M-P2 EXACTLY 120 of 120 in combat; P8 37/37; M-P4 opacity 0.50, area 57.2%, the world moves 99.2% of centre-40% pixels (control outside the screen 99.8%); M-P3 roll fires in combat with the screen open (state BACKSTEP, 14 stamina spent); P4 0/30 then 60/60 with the screen still open; M-P5 equip_start -> 30 committed frames -> equip_end; E11 0 toasts in a fight; all seven surfaces draw.

GAMEPAD-ONLY REACHABILITY PASSES. Walked with nothing but a GameSir X2s standard-mapping descriptor through __HARNESS.gamepad(): START opens the interface, the left stick moves focus (inventory.row.bog-iron-maul), the D-PAD moves the column 1->0, A confirms, START closes to 'world'. No keyboard, no pointer, no new button in the closed action set.

The d-pad needed one build fix to work: input/gamepad.js maps the D-pad onto `move` only while `pad.uiMode` is set, and nothing was setting it for these screens. UISystem._surfaceChanged() now does, on every open and close including a pad-driven one.

PROBE BUG worth recording for the next agent: RealInput.pushGamepadState reads each button entry as `typeof v === 'number' ? {...} : {pressed: !!v}`. An OBJECT is truthy, so a released button written as {pressed:false} arrives as PRESSED — the first poll reports all seventeen buttons rising at once and none ever rises again. It looks exactly like a build whose menus ignore the pad. Pass booleans or numbers.

RI-UIX06 FIDELITY (tools/metrics/ui-metrics.mjs, 1280x720 and 1920x1080, DPR 1 and 2): FD1 stem 0.8 device px; FD2 stem 1.468 device px at DPR 2 — the check the item says the whole thing turns on, and the one an upscaled canvas fails; FD4 0 clipped/overflowing elements at all four configurations; FD5 panel screen-fraction drift 0.00%; FD7 7.32 effective bits, overdraw 1.016x. FD3 and FD6 were failing on my own measurement code and on a 1-px type size; both fixed, rerun in flight at hand-off.

B4 MISS FOUND AND FIXED: the screen body face was 17 px in 1080p units — 17 px at 1080p (under B4's 18 px floor) and 0.0157 of screen height at 720p (under the 1.6% floor). It missed BOTH legs by a hair, in the direction nobody looks. game/src/ui/type.js BODY now holds the three body sizes in one place: screen 19, book 26, label 15.
next_step: Fresh independent reviewer-editor re-criticises the materially edited orchestration/plans/W1-21.md plan.
notes_for_successor: The one thing that must not regress: UISurface.el() is the ONLY drawing entry point and it clips the callback to the rect it declared, so the census and the pixels cannot disagree. If someone adds a raw ctx accessor, RI-UIX02 K2 stops meaning anything. Screens are pure functions of a model assembled in UISystem._*Model(); the engine's _uiCtx() is the only place that reads the simulation.
